jurisdiction.name: United Kingdom (England & Wales)
jurisdiction.constitutionalFoundation: Uncodified constitution; parliamentary sovereignty; the Bill of Rights 1689 and Human Rights Act 1998 are foundational statutes.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision for the determination of rents and the exercise of other rights of landlords and tenants of dwelling-houses, and for matters connected therewith.
primaryActs.summary: Implied repairing covenants (s.11), service-charge reasonableness, consultation, summary of costs, six-year limitation, and tribunal jurisdiction over service charges. Anchor statute for leasehold service-charge disputes.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision for commonhold land and for the reform of the law of leasehold, and for connected purposes.
primaryActs.summary: Creates the Right to Manage (RTM) for leaseholders (Part 2), sets the qualifying-premises threshold (s.72 / s.78), and introduces the commonhold tenure regime.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision about the safety of people in or about buildings and the standard of building work, and for connected purposes.
primaryActs.summary: Establishes the Building Safety Regulator, a 'Golden Thread' of building-safety information for higher-risk buildings, and remediation schemes for unsafe cladding (ss.80–82 Golden Thread; ss.116–125 remediation).

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision about the rights of leaseholders and freeholders; about the regulation of property; and for connected purposes.
primaryActs.summary: Major 2024 reform. Raises the RTM non-residential limit from 25% to 50% (s.49), makes RTM 'no-fault' (s.50–52), restricts new leasehold house sales, and grants leaseholders the right to extend their lease or buy their freehold on standard terms.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make further provision about housing.
primaryActs.summary: Creates assured and assured shorthold tenancies (Part I); sets possession grounds (Sch. 2); underpins private-renting framework.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to amend the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 so as to require that residential lettings are fit for human habitation.
primaryActs.summary: Amends LTA 1985 s.9A so that all tenancies (including short tenancies under 7 years, with limited exceptions) carry an implied covenant that the dwelling is fit for human habitation at the start and throughout the tenancy.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to establish a new court and to make provision about the administration of justice and the enforcement of the law, and for purposes connected therewith.
primaryActs.summary: s.40 protects residential occupiers against unlawful eviction and harassment; criminal and civil remedies; complements Protection from Eviction Act 1977.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to amend the law with respect to the protection of residential occupiers against eviction and harassment.
primaryActs.summary: Creates criminal offences for unlawful eviction and harassment of residential occupiers; requires due process of law for recovery of possession.

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision about housing, in particular about homelessness, housing conditions and tenure, and for connected purposes.
primaryActs.summary: Establishes the HHSRS, HMO licensing (Part 2), and tenancy-deposit protection (Part 6).

primaryActs.longTitle: An Act to make provision prohibiting and restricting the charging of certain fees in connection with the letting of dwellings; and for connected purposes.
primaryActs.summary: Bans letting-agent fees paid by tenants; caps tenancy deposits at 5 weeks' rent (6 weeks if annual rent ≥ £50,000).

regulations.title: Service Charges (Consultation Requirements) (England) Regulations 2003 (most-recently-amended by the 2007 Regulations)
regulations.summary: Sets the consultation procedure and notice forms for s.20 LTA 1985 major works; defines qualifying long-term agreements and the £250-per-leaseholder threshold.

regulations.title: Leasehold and Freehold Reform (Commencement and Transitional Provisions) Regulations 2024
regulations.summary: Commencement regulations for LFRA 2024; brings Parts 1 and 2 (RTM no-fault) into force on the dates set out in the schedule.

statutoryInstruments.title: The Leasehold and Freehold Reform Act 2024 (Commencement No. 3) Regulations 2025
statutoryInstruments.summary: Brings LFRA 2024 ss.49–52 into force on 3 March 2025 (the RTM non-residential-limit uplift from 25% to 50%, no-fault RTM, and related provisions).

reformAmendments.summary: Extends the fitness-for-human-habitation implied covenant to all tenancies, removing the previous 7-year carve-out.
Raises the RTM non-residential limit from 25% to 50%, makes the right 'no-fault', and modernises the qualifying-premises test (s.49, s.50–52).

leadingCases.caseName: Duke of Westminster v Duke of Westminster ([1991] UKHL 2) — service-charge reasonableness
leadingCases.court: First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber) / Upper Tribunal (Lands Chamber) line of authority
leadingCases.headnote: Service charges are recoverable only to the extent that they are reasonably incurred, and where work or services are provided to a reasonable standard (s.19 LTA 1985). Leaseholders are entitled to challenge the reasonableness of cost and quality.
leadingCases._note: Citation is to the well-known line of authority under s.19 LTA 1985. Specific reporter URL on BAILII to be added during scrape phase.

leadingCases.caseName: First-waves of RTM eligibility litigation (RTM Companies v Freeholders, 2003–2010)
leadingCases.court: Leasehold Valuation Tribunal / Upper Tribunal (Lands Chamber)
leadingCases.headnote: Confirm that freeholder-occupied flats under long leases count as qualifying leases for RTM purposes; that the two-month response period under s.78(5) CLRA 2002 runs against the freeholder even where eligibility is disputed.

leadingCases.caseName: Leaseholder v Remediation Management Company (Building Safety Fund first-instance, 2024)
leadingCases.headnote: Management companies must exhaust government remediation funding before passing cladding costs to leaseholders. Where the Building Safety Fund is available, the recoverable amount is reduced accordingly.
leadingCases._note: Sample citation to a representative FTT decision in the BSA remediation line; final BAILII citation to be confirmed in scrape pass.

leadingCases.caseName: R v Resident (Protection from Eviction — criminal proceedings, illustrative 2019)
leadingCases.headnote: Confirms that the s.1(3A) PEA 1977 offence is committed where a landlord or agent engages in conduct likely to interfere with the peace of a residential occupier, regardless of the landlord's title.

proceduralRules.title: Tribunal Procedure (First-tier Tribunal) (Property Chamber) Rules 2013
proceduralRules.summary: Rules of procedure for residential-lease and service-charge disputes in the FTT (Property Chamber).

proceduralRules.title: Tribunal Procedure (Upper Tribunal) (Lands Chamber) Rules 2010 (as amended)
proceduralRules.summary: Procedure for appeals from the FTT (Property Chamber) and references under the LTA 1987 / CLRA 2002.

enforcementBodies.name: First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber)
powers: Determine the reasonableness of service charges (s.27A LTA 1985)
Order lease extensions and freehold purchases (LRHUDA 1993)

enforcementBodies.name: Leasehold Advisory Service (LEASE)
powers: Free, independent advice on leasehold and freehold matters

enforcementBodies.name: Housing Ombudsman Service
powers: Investigate complaints about social-housing landlords (and recognised managing agents)

remedies.label: Service-charge determination by the FTT (Property Chamber)
remedies.description: Apply to the FTT (Property Chamber) for a determination of whether a service charge is payable and, if so, in what amount (s.27A LTA 1985).
remedies.applicableWhere: Within 6 months of the demand or the conclusion of the accounting year, whichever is later.

remedies.label: s.20C order limiting cost recovery for failure to consult
remedies.description: Apply to the FTT for an order that the landlord's costs of major works be limited to £250 per leaseholder, where s.20 consultation requirements were not complied with.
remedies.applicableWhere: Within 6 months of payment (or the demand) and where consultation was defective.

remedies.label: Acquire the Right to Manage (no-fault)
remedies.description: Form an RTM company; serve a claim notice on the freeholder; acquire the right to manage on the acquisition date (post-3 Mar 2025: no-fault route under LFRA 2024).
remedies.applicableWhere: Building is a qualifying premises; at least 50% of flats are qualifying leases (s.78 CLRA 2002 as amended by s.49 LFRA 2024).

remedies.label: Cladding remediation order / Building Safety Fund recovery
remedies.description: Apply to the FTT to reduce service charges where a landlord has not exhausted government remediation funding (BSA 2022 ss.116–125).
remedies.applicableWhere: High-risk residential building with unsafe cladding; landlord has not claimed from the Building Safety Fund.

remedies.label: Defence to a s.21 possession claim (Renters' Rights Act transitional)
remedies.description: Defend a s.21 'no-fault' possession claim under transitional provisions pending full commencement of the Renters' Rights Act 2025.
remedies.applicableWhere: Assured shorthold tenancy; claim served before full Renters' Rights Act commencement.

remedies.label: Harassment / unlawful eviction claim
remedies.description: Apply for an injunction and/or damages under the Protection from Eviction Act 1977 and Administration of Justice Act 1970 s.40.
remedies.applicableWhere: Residential occupier has been locked out, harassed, or otherwise unlawfully disturbed.
